title: New Orleans Wiggle and the Piron band's New York engagements
summary: Playing New Orleans Wiggle, he says brother Pete wrote it; recalls recording for three companies, Club Deluxe and offers from the Scandals.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Why don't we play one of the records now and you just tell us what you remember about them.
I think that's bouncing around eh? No, I don't think so. Who's that the box haven't you heard? This is New Orleans Wiggle. I'm thinking it's New Orleans Wiggle. That's it, yup. New Orleans Wiggle.
That's right. Well that number was written by my brother, Pete.
Who did he arrange it on?

He did his stuff. Pete wrote it and arranged it. And of course when it was in New York I think it was published by Williams. I'm not positive, I don't know, I'm sure it was. I know West Indies Blues was published by Clarence, you know. And uh, we did that number on uh, I think, OK recording. If I'm not mistaken. Because we did record for OK, the Brumvicks and Victor people. Three companies. Three companies. And uh, of course that's Teo that's clarinet you're hearing there. We had nine men in the orchestra and uh, according to the critics we had, considered one of the finest orchestras to hit New York at that time, you know. And uh, we played the uh, well it wasn't the Cotton Club then, it was Club Deluxe. It was owned by former heavyweight champion Jack Johnson and a man by the name of Levy. Then we played a one week's uh, tryout at Lafayette during the closing of the club for a redecoration period. And during that week we had critics who hit us, you see. And we had offers to go with uh, Joy's White Scandals. Which they torn down, the men didn't want to stay in New York. Also another big job in uh, a big summer resort I think it was in Bridgeport, Connecticut.
